items.title: Dark Keynote Product-Proof Deck
items.description: A DARK KEYNOTE / PRODUCT-PROOF DECK SYSTEM (16:9) built as repeatable layouts. TRUE-BLACK #050607 ground so a single EMERALD #35e0a0 RADIAL GLOW entering from one edge reads as emitted light; MONOSPACE metadata; an INVERTED WHITE PILL as the primary CTA; a heavy-sans hero (Archivo Black, Inter-Black fallback); a faint film-grain overlay on every slide. Layouts: COVER (mono eyebrow + heavy-sans headline bottom-left + white pill), PRODUCT-PROOF (a self-built UI mock in BROWSER CHROME with KPI tiles, accent numbers in emerald - the product demonstrates itself), and a METRIC slide (one over-specified number like 66.0879% with an emerald spike). Palette is strictly black + white + one emerald. Reusable for SaaS/product keynotes, launch and demo decks, investor pitches, and dark product-marketing covers.

items.title: Minimal Swiss Field-Notes Deck
items.description: A MINIMAL SWISS / INTERNATIONAL-STYLE DECK SYSTEM (16:9) built as repeatable layouts. Cool paper #e9ecee ground, near-black ink, and ONE ultramarine #1c39c4 spike as the only accent. The rule that governs everything: emphasis comes from WEIGHT + COLOR, never SIZE - one calm type size, meaning carried by a bolder weight and a few ultramarine words/numbers. Content is held in a wide LEFT column with a large empty margin; a single HAIRLINE RULE is the only ornament. Layouts: COVER (mono rail + hairline + weight-emphasis headline), NUMBERED AGENDA (01-04 in tabular-nums ultramarine, hairline-separated rows), and a PLAYFAIR closer line. Reusable for design/engineering reviews, field-notes decks, quiet product updates, and any considered, restrained presentation.

items.title: Editorial Magazine Pitch Deck
items.description: An EDITORIAL MAGAZINE PITCH-DECK SYSTEM (16:9) built as repeatable layouts, not one slide. Off-white #f1ece1 ground, ONE brick-red #b3401f accent, and a low film-grain overlay on every slide. The signature is one ENORMOUS Anton condensed word (Oswald/Archivo-Narrow fallback) as the cover hero, packed tight (line-height ~.8) so the type fills the frame, plus TRACKED-CAPS editorial furniture (label left / year right) pinned to the top margin that REPEATS on every content slide as the through-line. Layouts: COVER (giant word-stack + byline), CONTENT/STAT (a huge Anton number over a short editorial line), and a SECTION BREAK that inverts to a solid brick-red ground with a Playfair Display serif for the register shift. Reusable for pitch decks, quarterly/brand reviews, magazine-style report covers, and lookbooks.

items.title: Data Report Deck: Narrow Rail and a Real Eight-Row Table at Poster Scale
items.description: A dense report deck that actually holds data. An unequal 30/70 split puts a narrow saturated rail down the left carrying identity, one statistic and a pull quote, while the wide field takes a heavy display headline and a genuine eight-row table with a totals rule. Bone and rust, flat fields, tabular figures throughout. Good for estate and operations reports, quarterly reviews, board packs, and any deck that has to survive someone reading the numbers.

items.title: Poster Deck: Rotated Colour Band Carrying the Headline, Sunflower and Indigo
items.description: A loud two-colour event deck built around a single band rotated off-axis that runs out of both side edges and carries the headline inside it. The band is the layout, not a decoration: it turns 90 degrees into a panel divider on the content slide, and the closer inverts ground and ink. Heavy geometric monospace display type, hand-drawn squiggles and one hard-shadowed sticker badge do the rest. Good for zine fairs, markets, club nights, workshops, student shows and any programme that should feel printed rather than filed.

items.title: Catalogue Deck: Script Crossing Through a Rounded Display Headline
items.description: A warm catalogue deck whose signature is a script line crossing straight THROUGH the giant rounded headline as a layer, not sitting under it as a caption. A full-height flat panel holds the deck's furniture down one side while the type field rags left, so the split is asymmetric rather than centred. Butter, deep teal and one tomato accent. Good for product catalogues, stationery and craft studios, menus, small-brand lookbooks and any deck that should feel made by hand rather than shipped by a template.

items.title: Ledger Deck: Two Colours That Swap Roles, Against a Full-Height Shelf Column
items.description: A two-colour ledger deck where the same pair swaps jobs partway through — saturated ground with pale ink for two slides, then the closer flips them — so the ending reads as a change of register without introducing a single new colour. A full-height column of flat vertical bars runs down one side as the structural rail, and the title word is sliced by the top edge, then by the bottom. Good for studio and workshop reports, craft-business year notes, portfolio intros and any deck that wants to look printed.

items.title: Editorial Report Deck: Migrating Colour Band with an Edge-Cropped Headline
items.description: A field-report deck where one flat colour band moves position from slide to slide — top on the cover, bottom on the data slide, full-bleed on the closer — so the deck reads as a single field being re-cut rather than three separate pages. The title word is sliced by the frame's horizontal edge, deliberately, and a condensed poster face does all the shouting while a plain grotesque handles every functional label. Two colours only, one of them carrying all the ink. Good for research reports, field notes, annual reviews, survey findings and any deck whose credibility comes from looking measured rather than sold.
